evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學人文電算研究中心）
evidence.text: The entry describes Spring and Autumn bronze 半 as 八 plus 牛: 八 is said to indicate division and also serve as a phonetic element, while 牛 represents the object divided. It proposes ‘split/open’ as an original sense extended to ‘half,’ but gives no dated sequence for that semantic development. It attributes the proposal that 半 is an early form of 判 to 何琳儀.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學人文電算研究中心）
evidence.text: The entry reports Spring and Autumn/Warring States variants substituting 斗 or 升 for 牛, interpreted as measuring vessels that suggest a half measure, and a variant substituting shape-similar 刃 for 斗, described as a phonetic element. The page does not establish exact dates or a complete order for these forms.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢字構形資料庫, Academia Sinica
evidence.text: The record labels a bronze example 集成04315 and a Small Seal/說文 form, and interprets the graph as 八 indicating division with 牛 as the ox divided. The page does not itself provide a primary transcription or establish the precise date of the cited graph; no glyph pixels were visually inspected.
evidence.title: 漢字「半」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學人文電算研究中心）
evidence.text: The entry reports a bronze numeral use meaning ‘half’ and cites 秦公簋 wording 一斗七升大半升. The cited database discussion does not independently date the semantic transition from ‘split’ to ‘half’; the entry’s gloss sequence cannot establish chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（香港中文大學人文電算研究中心）
evidence.text: The entry reports 半 in the Mawangdui Zhouyi, Tun line 27, where the received text has 磐桓, and treats 半 as a loan graph for 磐. This is whole-graph reuse for another word, distinct from the proposed phonetic role of 八 inside 半. The page does not establish the manuscript token’s exact pronunciation or the reason for the spelling.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction dataset
evidence.text: The supplied local Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows give 八: Middle Chinese transcription peat, Old Chinese *pˤret; 半: Middle Chinese transcription panH, Old Chinese *pˤan-s. Their Old Chinese forms share an initial but differ in their endings. This comparison is compatible with a possible sound relation but does not by itself establish 八’s role in 半. Local provenance: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, exact character rows 八 and 半. The dataset PDF search result was found, but opening the PDF returned a 502 error; these values are reported from the supplied local rows, not from an opened PDF.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

gaps: The candidate Commons seal glyph could not be inspected, so identity, provenance, dating scope, and rights remain unverified; no glyph should be selected from this lead on filename evidence alone.
No primary image or transcription of the cited 集成04315 inscription was inspected; the reading and date of that individual occurrence remain database-reported.

CUHK’s semantic proposal from ‘split/open’ to ‘half’ remains undated. The earliest attested spoken-word sense and chronology of midpoint, partial/incomplete, and ‘very little’ senses remain unresolved.
八’s phonetic role is an explicit database analysis, but the checked Baxter–Sagart forms differ in their endings; no explanation of that correspondence was established.
The 判 initial-graph claim is attributed to 何琳儀, but the original publication and its full argument were not inspected.
The Mawangdui 半-for-磐 spelling remains a source-reported whole-graph loan; the token was not checked against a primary facsimile and its precise Han-period sound correspondence remains unestablished.

Official Unicode per-character kMandarin pages and the Baxter–Sagart PDF failed to open. Local readings are recorded with local-file provenance and are not presented as externally verified exact-row evidence.
